description: Stay Radar tuning. Config, never code: everything an operator might reasonably change lives here. Provider-specific knowledge does NOT belong here — a provider that needs a setting reads its own env.

observation.currencyNote: One pinned request currency so every baseline is single-currency. Phase 8h (2026-08-28): switched USD->EUR for the trip-market comparison set - the package sellers quote EUR natively and Xotelo/Agoda/SerpAPI all accept EUR, so future comparable stay observations collect EUR directly instead of riding FX. Currency is a hard baseline dimension: EUR baselines start fresh from here, USD history remains valid (and reaches EUR comparisons through the stored-FX layer); nothing is converted in place, and old USD rows are never re-quoted just to normalize them.
observation.defaultNightsNote: Used only when a property has no typicalStayNights; the observe loop prefers the property's own typical lengths.
observation.politeDelayNote: Pause between consecutive requests to the same free service. Xotelo is donation-run; being cheap is the point, being rude is not.
observation.maxRequestsPerRunNote: Hard ceiling on external requests per observe invocation, reserve-before-await style: the loop stops planning work it has no budget to perform. CLI --limit may lower but never raise it.

sanity.nightlyNote: Floors catch data errors ($0, $3), NOT good deals — a genuinely absurd bargain at a real property is the entire point of this system and must survive sanity. Ceilings catch unit errors (a stay total or minor-unit amount recorded as a nightly).

sampling.rotationNote: Successive runs interleave BETWEEN the previous run's grid points (flight-radar pattern) so a week of runs covers the horizon finely without any single run brute-forcing it. Deterministic on (anchor date, runIndex): dry-run shows the exact real run.
sampling.calendarEveryNRunsNote: A calendar covers ~90 forward days in one request, so it does not need refreshing every run. Offset per property so calendar load spreads across runs.

targeted.cheapWindowNote: The sparse grid is blind between its points; the provider's own calendar is not. Each run may add up to this many samples aimed at runs of >= minCheapRunNights consecutive 'cheap' days in the latest calendar — the exact windows worth watching.
targeted.neighborNote: An unusually low observation (>= neighborTriggerPercentBelow under its own median) earns neighboring check-in samples: an isolated glitch and a bookable cheap window look identical until the dates around it are observed.
targeted.recentSampleCooldownNote: Never re-ask a (property, check-in) the radar sampled within this many days — targeted sampling must add NEW information, not burn budget re-measuring.

budgets.confirmationDelayNote: Minimum pause before each confirmation-tier request. The confirmation source is unofficial and replaceable; one polite request per trigger, no retries, ever — a failed confirmation is a recorded fact, not a retry loop.
budgets.breakerNote: Consecutive TRANSPORT failures (network/HTTP-level, not semantic errors) trip a per-provider circuit breaker for the cooldown. Semantic errors never trip it — an API saying 'bad params' proves the transport works.

trigger.description: Decides ONLY whether one confirmation request is worth spending. Not an alert score — Phase 8c owns scoring.
trigger.calendarCheapFractionNote: At least this fraction of the stay's nights must be classified 'cheap' in the LATEST calendar observation for the property. Half the stay cheap = worth one look; one lucky night is not.
trigger.conservativeNote: Below minSamplesForMedian prior observations the median rule stays silent (no evidence, no spend); the calendar rule may still fire because it is the provider's own cross-date comparison, not ours.

anomaly.noHistoryScoreCapNote: A decision with no baseline behind it is judged on absolute price and evidence alone; dropping the history components concentrates the surviving weights, so without a cap an unevidenced rate could outrank one backed by dozens of observations. 80, below the flight radar's 85, because stay history is younger and thinner.

baseline.maxBaselineAgeNote: A baseline whose NEWEST member is older than this is an archive, not a comparison — no baseline is emitted.
baseline.staleBaselineNote: Newest member older than this (but within max): baseline stands, confidence is knocked down one tier and STALE_BASELINE is recorded.
baseline.relaxationNote: The ONLY safe relaxation: stay-length bucket, because the comparison unit is already per-night. Property, source_class, room_class, board, occupancy and currency are hard dimensions and are never relaxed — a meta quote is not a retail room, an AI rate is not a breakfast rate, and 2-adult pricing is not 4-adult pricing.

anomaly.weightsNote: The four concepts of the judgement, each 0..1 before weighting. Uncomputable components are dropped and the weights renormalise; a component that RAN and said 'ordinary' scores 0 and KEEPS its weight. A property may be interesting from the relative path OR the absolute path alone — neither requires the other — but candidacy (70) needs a strong path PLUS real evidence and a usable window: a strong relative anomaly maxes ~50 meta-only, ~57 with an Agoda confirmation (gate territory), and crosses 70 only verified + actionable. A property whose LOW price is its NORMAL price is not a mispricing and deliberately tops out below 70.

relativeComposition.note: Inside the relative concept: how far below the property's own median, plus where the rate sits in the distribution. Percentile credit is SCALED BY BASELINE MATURITY (the confidence tier value): being the lowest of five observations is a fact about five observations, not about the property.

anomaly.lowPercentileNote: Full percentile credit at the 0th percentile, zero credit at the 25th and above — being merely below median is not remarkable.

actionability.notablePriceNote: Persistence must never rescue an ordinary price: unless the rate is notably low (relative >= minNotableRelative, or an absolute rule fired), actionability scores a REAL ZERO — the component ran and found nothing actionable about an ordinary rate lasting a week.

evidenceValues.note: A meta (Xotelo) observation whose property+window has a same-window retail confirmation on record is worth more than a bare meta sighting, but never as much as the retail observation itself. A metered (SerpAPI) verification on record for the window sits above the free confirmation and below being the verified observation.

crossSource.retailSpreadNote: When the cheapest same-window retail nightly exceeds the meta nightly by more than this percent, the candidate carries RETAIL_SPREAD_HIGH: the meta price may not be bookable at retail. Recorded as a fact and a caution badge — never used to blend the two numbers.

verification.description: The gate in front of every METERED hotel verification call. A random observation must never reach SerpAPI: only near-threshold candidates with a nameable reason spend money, and the reason is recorded BEFORE the request.
verification.nearMissNote: Only candidates scoring >= candidateThreshold - nearMissBand are considered at all — a floor, not the gate itself: qualification still requires a strong sub-score reason below.
verification.monthlyBudgetNote: The stay radar's OWN SerpAPI allowance (provider 'serpapi_hotels', counted separately). It shares the API key but NEVER the flight radar's budget or manual reserve — exhausting this stops stay verification and touches nothing else. Override with STAYS_SERPAPI_MONTHLY_BUDGET.
verification.opportunityCooldownNote: One paid verification per opportunity (price-free key) per cooldown — re-observing the same cheap week must not re-spend.

calendarSignal.note: A flip is: the LATEST per-date classification says cheap while an EARLIER snapshot within the lookback said average/high for the same date. Supporting evidence only.

category.description: The second absolute-value axis: where does this nightly sit in the CROSS-PROPERTY distribution of the same category (destination group × board × luxury tier × source class × tax status × currency)? A stay can be objectively exceptional for its category even when it is normal for its property. The judged property's own rows are EXCLUDED — a category of one is a mirror, not a market.
category.lowPercentileNote: Full credit at the category's 0th percentile, zero at the 15th and above — only the genuine cheap tail of the category counts.
category.maturityNote: Category credit is scaled by the same confidence tiers as property baselines: a 20-sample two-property category speaks softly.

absolute.derivationNote: Initial thresholds derived 2026-08-28 from the radar's own first observations, set CONSERVATIVELY BELOW observed normals so ordinary pricing cannot fire them: Maldives AI luxury observed $870–1,010/nt normal with a $681 cheap-season low (Lily Beach); Riviera Maya AI luxury observed $1,087–1,390 (Grand Velas); Maldives ultra any-board observed $2,400–4,300 typical (Soneva, breakfast basis). Groups without observations yet (Bali, Thailand, Los Cabos, Seychelles-Mauritius) got deliberately strict bars that only truly absurd prices can cross; they should be revisited as history accumulates. All bars assume per-night per-room 2-adult USD; taxes-unknown meta quotes cross the same bars (a tax-in price crossing is stronger — the evidence layer records which it was). RESTATED IN EUR 2026-08-28 (Phase 8h currency switch): policy thresholds re-authored from the USD bars at the stored ECB reference rate 0.85874 (fx_rate_observations #1, 2026-08-27), rounded DOWN so every bar stays at least as strict as its USD original. Policy numbers, not converted observations - USD-era decisions already stored keep their USD basis.
absolute.tierScaleNote: An ultra property's 'cheap' sits far above a luxury property's — the same bar cannot serve Soneva and a 5* chain. Scales multiply the rule thresholds.
absolute.roomScaleNote: Applied only when the observation carries a room class (retail tiers do; meta property-level quotes do not): a villa crossing the bar is a stronger fact than an entry room crossing it, so the villa's bar sits higher. Unknown/absent room class uses 1.0.
